title: WhatToLookAt: learned relations become a sensing budget
summary: WhatToLookAt takes the history-written relation machinery from SighImageFactorization and asks a compressed-sensing-style engineering question: if experience has already learned useful structure, how many future physical observations can be omitted? Gates 0–4 turn learned relations into an explicit adaptive sensing budget and then into a falsifiable compression hypothesis. Gate 5 measures the price of sparse measurement rows. Gate 6 separates sparse sensing that is designed sparse from a dense operator that is pruned afterward, showing that support coverage itself can be part of the sensing algorithm.

nodes.claim: Learns persistent relations from past temporal structure and uses them as a prior for future sparse sensing; local relation uncertainty withdraws sharing authority and purchases extra measurements only where confidence is low.
nodes.survived: Learned relations can replace future observations in controlled worlds; charged image-derived confidence and current residuals localize when extra sensing is needed; Gate 5 measures a nontrivial sparse-measurement frontier; and Gate 6 shows that coverage-designed sparse sensing can match the post-hoc-pruned quality frontier with four times fewer guide coordinate touches in a one-coordinate innovation regime.
nodes.killed: Blind trust, shuffled confidence, coordinate memory and equal-cost random extra reads fail their matched controls. Extreme row sparsity is not free, and Gate 6 also kills the assumption that pruning a previously dense measurement operator is equivalent to designing its sparse support before observation: post-hoc pruning needs substantially more rows to close support blind spots.

edges.why: WhatToLookAt explicitly states that it pushes the compressed-sensing question into the SighImageFactorization/Sihti lineage and operationalizes SighImageFactorization's learned relation state as a prior that can reduce future sensing.

WhatToLookAt explicitly names Sihti in its lineage and carries forward the operator-dependent-structure framing, but does not claim Sihti code inheritance; the new currency is measurement cost rather than residue location.
